name: @w6w-apps/docuseal
description: Build DocuSeal templates, send submissions for signature, manage submitters, and read completed documents.

w6w.longDescription:
DocuSeal is an open-source document signing platform, and this app covers its two hosted API hosts — the templates that define what gets signed, and the submissions that send them out and track who has signed. A template can be built from an HTML fragment with inline field tags, from a PDF or DOCX with fields placed by coordinate, or created and updated through the Studio UI and then driven from here by id; templates can also be cloned or merged into a new one. A submission turns a template (or a fresh set of documents) into a live signature request for one or more submitters, in a fixed or parallel signing order, and this app covers the whole lifecycle — creating it, listing and reading submissions and their documents, updating or archiving one, and reading or updating an individual submitter's own record (including re-sending their invite or marking them signed on their behalf).

DocuSeal hosts every account on one of two fixed API hosts — the global service or the EU one — chosen once at connect time; nothing about the account moves between them afterward. Deliberately out of scope: uploading documents outside a submission/template call (this app sends base64 content or a downloadable URL, exactly as the API accepts, never a local file the sandbox cannot produce), and the vendor's self-hosted deployment path, since the two hosted API hosts are the only ones this app's network allowlist can name.
